# Template: ray_diagram
A thin-lens ray diagram with the geometry COMPUTED from the thin-lens equation 1/f = 1/d + 1/dᵢ: object arrow, lens, both focal points, the two principal rays (parallel→through F, and straight through the centre), and the image. A converging lens (default) makes a real, inverted image when the object is outside f, a virtual, upright, dashed one (rays traced back) when it is inside f, and no image at all with the object exactly at f (the rays leave parallel); a diverging lens (lens_type) always makes a small, upright, virtual image. Choose this scene for ANY request about lenses, ray diagrams, image formation, real vs virtual images, magnification, a magnifying glass, a camera, projector or eye lens, or "what happens when the object moves inside the focal length". Vary focal_length and object_distance and the figure re-derives itself — rescaled to fit on every frame unless `view` fixes the scale: set view to animate the object THROUGH the focal point, so the object really moves and the image runs off to infinity and comes back virtual. Paused, the viewer drags the object (distance and height) and either F (the focal length), and with show_distances scrubs or taps the d and f numbers; every value recomputes live ({lens.di}, m, do, f, image_kind: 1 real, −1 virtual, 0 none).
Parameter schema:
{
 "type": "object",
 "properties": {
  "focal_length": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Focal length in arbitrary units (default 10), always positive; lens_type says which way it bends."
  },
  "object_distance": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Object distance from the lens, same units (default 25). Less than focal_length gives a virtual image; equal gives none."
  },
  "object_height": {
   "type": "number",
   "description": "Object height in units (default 6)."
  },
  "lens_type": {
   "type": "string",
   "enum": [
    "converging",
    "diverging"
   ],
   "description": "converging (convex, default) or diverging (concave: the image is always virtual, upright and smaller)."
  },
  "show_labels": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "F / object / image labels (default true)."
  },
  "show_distances": {
   "type": "boolean",
   "description": "Dimension marks under the axis on the object's side: d (object to lens) and f (F to lens), as numbers the viewer can scrub or tap (default false)."
  },
  "view": {
   "type": "object",
   "description": "Fix the scale: the axis units shown left and right of the lens, and the height above the axis the page holds. Without it the figure refits to every object distance; set it (e.g. {left: 30, right: 45, height: 8}) to animate object_distance through f. The live drag sets it.",
   "properties": {
    "left": {
     "type": "number"
    },
    "right": {
     "type": "number"
    },
    "height": {
     "type": "number"
    }
   },
   "required": [
    "left",
    "right"
   ]
  }
 }
}
Element ids your commands can reference:
- axis: the optical axis
- lens: the lens (double-headed arrow; arrowheads turned inward for a diverging lens)
- focal_left / focal_right: the focal-point ticks
- object: the object arrow
- ray_parallel: the parallel-then-through-focus principal ray
- ray_center: the straight-through-center principal ray
- ray_parallel_ext / ray_center_ext: dashed back-extensions, present only when the image is virtual (ray_center_ext only for a converging lens)
- image: the image arrow (dashed when virtual); absent with the object at f, where there is no image
- label_object / label_image / label_left / label_right: the labels (label_left and label_right are the two F labels)
- do_mark / do_value: the object-distance dimension arrow and its "d = 25" number (show_distances)
- f_mark / f_value: the focal-length dimension arrow and its "f = 10" number (show_distances)
Examples:
Request: "Draw a ray diagram for a converging lens with the object outside the focal length." → params: {"focal_length":10,"object_distance":25,"object_height":6}
Request: "Show why a magnifying glass makes a virtual image when the object is inside the focal length." → params: {"focal_length":12,"object_distance":7,"object_height":5}
Request: "Why does a diverging lens always make a smaller, upright image?" → params: {"focal_length":10,"object_distance":20,"object_height":6,"lens_type":"diverging"}
Request: "Move the object in through the focal point and watch the image flip." → params: {"focal_length":10,"object_distance":25,"object_height":4,"show_distances":true,"view":{"left":30,"right":45,"height":8}}

Viewer can: Drag the object (distance and height) or either F (focal length); the rays and the image follow, running off to infinity at F and coming back virtual.

In YAML: `template: ray_diagram` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
